question.prompt: What is the constant term in the expansion of \((x+1)^6\)?

solutions.explanation: The constant term contains no \(x\), meaning the exponent of \(x\) is 0. Its coefficient is \(C(6,6)=1\).
solutions.title: Select the term with no x

solutions.explanation:
The constant term is the only term of a polynomial that remains when \(x=0\), since all positive powers of \(x\) vanish. Therefore the constant term of \((x+1)^6\) is
\[
(0+1)^6=1.
\]
solutions.title: Evaluate at zero
